title: Altered Carbon — Player Character Sheet Guide

pages.name: 00 — Your first five minutes
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Start Here

Open your character

Open Actors and double-click the character assigned to you, or double-click your token. Start on Overview. The character sheet is your operational interface: you can roll, use equipment, update current resources and clear conditions without unlocking the entire sheet.

Before your first roll

  1. Describe what you want to achieve and agree the Skill and Difficulty with the GM.
  2. For an ordinary task, use a Roll button in Skills or Fast Skill Checks.
  3. For a weapon attack, target the enemy token, then use the weapon’s Attack / Use button in Equipped Systems or Loadout. A Firearms Skill roll alone is a Check, rather than a complete weapon attack.
  4. Confirm Zone, ammunition and any required Specialisation or modifiers. In combat, select the Active Speed Dice the action spends.
  5. Read chat. The natural Skill Die, Target Result and Degrees determine what you can resolve. The target responds before Damage.

Your identity survives your body

Your DHF is your persistent mind and identity. A sleeve is the body you currently inhabit. Wounds and Health describe the sleeve; Ego describes your mind. Sleeve death and destruction of a cortical stack are different events. The GM separately adjudicates Real Death.

pages.name: 01 — Header, resources and the lock
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

The top of the sheet

Portrait and identity

The portrait, true name, public name, archetype and variant identify the character. STACK, SLEEVE and EGO status chips show current integrity. The clock opens the future calendar and your viewing time zone.

Current values are editable

ReadoutMeaningHow to use it
Health / maximumPhysical integrity (HP).Click the current number to record HP loss or recovery. The maximum stays protected.
Wounds / thresholdAccumulated trauma. Threshold normally equals Strength, with specific modifiers.Edit current Wounds when directed, or use queued combat damage. Wounds may exceed the threshold; it is not a hard cap. Above it, further Wounds lose HP.
Ego / available maximumDHF and mental integrity (EP). Permanent loss reduces the available maximum.Edit current EP for a frag, trauma, recovery or GM instruction. Use Clinical for source-specific Ego-loss events.
SPStack Points: growth, recovery and exceptional resilience.Edit the current balance or use Spend / Level Up. Costs should follow a resolved rule or GM award.
IPInfluence Points: social leverage and Requests.Edit the current balance for an agreed cost or award. The base maximum is protected by Edit Sheet.
WealthAbstract purchasing power; not a cash wallet.The main readout is effective Wealth after relevant modifiers. Edit Sheet changes its base total.
Speed DiceThe d6 pool used for timing and action costs.In combat the counter shows used / total. Use the tactical console to select, lock or spend dice.

Edit Sheet

The lock protects base Attributes, maxima and descriptive fields. It does not lock current Health, Wounds, Ego, SP, IP, Deferral or Debt. Edit Sheet is for rebuilding or correcting base data. Save & Finish returns to normal play. Strength and Perception edits update the active sleeve itself. Use Current Sleeve to change its Health maximum. The Character Creator is in the Actors directory; it is not on an existing PC or NPC sheet.

pages.name: 02 — Overview panels
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Overview: your command deck

Integrity & Reserves

Health, Ego and Wounds meters show your current state; Defense, Protection, Speed, SP and IP summarize the numbers used during play. Defense makes an attack harder. Protection reduces incoming Wounds at Resolution. These are different defenses.

Condition Monitor

Each active condition is named. Open its entry to read the effect and duration, then use Clear after its published removal requirement is met or the GM directs you. Clearing does not spend a Move action or roll a recovery check automatically. Prone, Panic and other conditions still require the appropriate action/check before removal. Managed drug effects end through Clinical → Metabolize / End Encounter; Clear will point you there. Clearing Virtual exits the active Virtual session. Non-condition alerts, such as low Health or unresolved Wounds, remain until their underlying cause changes.

Fast Skill Checks

These are shortcuts to frequently used Skills. Roll opens a Check dialog. It does not assume a weapon, opponent or Damage profile. For an attack, use a weapon’s Attack button.

Equipped Systems

This panel lists ready gear. Attack uses a weapon’s tactical procedure. Use with Skill handles devices or software. Clinical Procedure opens drug administration and medical controls. Browse all equipment goes to Loadout.

DHF Profile & Resource Controls

Expand this panel for identity fields, current resource controls, Wealth, Deferral and Debt. Descriptors and base values need Edit Sheet. Attributes below it distinguish the physical sleeve (Strength, Perception) from the four persistent DHF Attributes.

pages.name: 03 — Skills and Check dialog
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Skills: stat high, roll low

Attribute groups

AttributeWhat it describes
StrengthPhysical power, endurance and damage tolerance.
PerceptionSenses and reactions in the sleeve. Its bonus sets the natural Speed Dice pool.
EmpathyRelating to other people and understanding their emotions.
WillpowerResolve and mental resistance.
AcuityInsight, intuition and investigation of underlying meaning.
IntelligenceReasoning, learning, knowledge and technical work.

Rows and rules

Each Skill row shows its Level and die. The Roll button rolls; the arrow expands the full rules, Specialisations, difficulty examples and Triggered Effects. Skill Levels 1–5 use d12, d10, d8, d6 and d4 respectively. A smaller die is better because you want a result at or below the Target Result.

Check options

Difficulty subtracts from the Target Result. The base is normally the relevant Attribute Bonus (the tens value), but the GM may set a scenario Target Result. Training, Gear and allowed modifiers raise it. The system does not stack multiple bonuses of the same non-stacking category. Bonus Dice are alternate results; pick the most favorable legal result. Luck Dice have a separate GM-selected procedure. Sight and context options tell the system when a conditional effect applies. Visibility determines who sees the Check.

Read the result

At the Target Result you gain one positive Degree. Below it, the difference supplies positive Degrees; above it, the difference supplies negative Degrees, capped at five of each. A natural 1 on the Skill Die is an Ace, automatically successful, with the Skill’s Special benefit. A 1 on a Bonus Die is not an Ace. Aces do not universally double Damage. A double natural 1 with a Luck Die creates a Stroke of Luck. A failing Skill Die and Luck Die both on their maximum faces cause a Catastrophe, which a successful Bonus Die does not erase.

Core references: pp.87–94.

pages.name: 04 — Combat and Speed Dice
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Combat: Intent → Check → Resolution

Intent and timing

  1. The GM starts a new Turn. Roll your Speed Dice privately.
  2. Choose the dice to make Active for this Round and lock the selection. Keep some in reserve if you want to defend later.
  3. The GM reveals everyone together. The lowest total on Active dice acts first.
  4. Use only your Active dice for your normal declared actions. A defensive Save may spend any available die, including reserve.
  5. After Active dice are resolved, remaining dice may be selected for another Round without rerolling. When all are spent, the next Turn begins.

Combat panel tools

Speed shows your action pool, Defense shows attack Difficulty, Damage Threshold shows the sleeve buffer, and Stack shows cortical integrity. Cover and Stance affect incoming attacks. Zone Assistant helps establish Shared, Adjacent or Distant range. The Combat Console controls phase, selections and reserve dice. Unarmed Attack uses Brawl; its -2 penalty applies against an armed or Battle Armored opponent unless a rule removes it.

Action costs

An ordinary Hit normally resolves at least one Active Speed Die. Select extra dice for drawing gear, movement or any printed additional cost. Attack automatically spends the selected dice and tracks the additional attack Difficulty for that Turn. You must record separate Move/Support costs in the console. Do not spend the same attack dice a second time. Other check-based actions and unusual printed costs remain GM-reviewed.

Range and positions

Shared does not automatically mean Engaged. Melee requires Engaged opponents in the Shared Zone. Adjacent normally adds 2 Difficulty; Distant adds 3 per Zone crossed, with weapon exceptions. A Hidden target must be revealed. Full Defense forgoes other Skill Checks and requires the attacker to roll a GM-selected Luck Die. Its Move cost and unusual stance/cover rulings are resolved with the GM.

Core references: pp.123–137.

pages.name: 05 — Attacks, defenses and Aces
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

From attack to Damage

Attack from your weapon

  1. Target the intended opponent before clicking Attack.
  2. Confirm range, Engaged if relevant, ammunition and action. Standard ammunition uses the weapon’s Depletion procedure.
  3. Confirm Check modifiers and required Speed Dice, then roll.
  4. If Accuracy allows repeated Hits, declare how many positive Degrees you plan to use. Accuracy repeats the complete Hit formula and applies its printed Save penalty when used more than once.
  5. The attack card states Potential Hit while the target or GM chooses a defense. Save Throw / Cancel Degrees subtracts the defender’s positive Degrees. A failed Save can grant extra Degrees of Difference to the attacker. Parry and Dodge can add Protection instead.
  6. After the defense is resolved or declined, a successful Hit exposes Roll Damage. The damage card belongs to this attack and original target.

Defense buttons

A Save Throw costs an available Speed Die. The dialog offers a Skill and GM-adjustable base TR. Dodge uses Athletics: Protection d8+PB against ranged attacks, d6+PB against melee, or d4+PB in Grapple. You can spend a Speed Die directly for one Dodge without rolling a Check. Parry requires Brawl or a weapon with Parry and only protects against melee. Model-specific Parry upgrades still need confirmation. Take Attack / No Defense declines the Save and leaves Defense and Armor in force.

What an Ace does

Firearms and Directed Energy Weapons add extra Wounds equal to Perception Bonus per resolved attack. Brawl and Melee Combat roll one additional Speed Die immediately. Weapon- and Trait-specific Ace clauses may add further effects and require a GM ruling. Neither a natural 1 nor the optional hit-location d12 means universally doubled Damage.

Read unusual results

Burst and fully automatic fire grant positive Degrees on Use even if the Skill Check also generates failure Degrees. Read both parts of the result. Special ammunition, Blast, Suppression, Charged Hit, Disarm and Stun use their own printed effects. Core Stun makes a target resolve required Speed Dice; it does not create a universal Stunned Condition. Use the GM-assisted special-effect controls for these cases.

Core references: pp.89–90, 100–105, 198–201.

pages.name: 06 — Wounds, Injuries and Dying
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Resolving damage and recovery

Queue first, resolve once

The target owner or GM uses Queue Resolution Wounds on incoming damage cards. The Combat panel then shows pending attacks and their total. At Resolution, click Resolve Wounds. Protection applies once to the aggregate, not separately to each normal attack. Dodge/Parry Protection is included. The default minimum is one Wound from damaging attacks. Mixed Armor Piercing or damage types require GM confirmation of effective Protection.

Wounds and Deadly

Wounds accumulate; each Wound beyond Damage Threshold loses HP. Deadly Wounds also directly lose HP in addition to counting as Wounds. Protection first reduces the non-Deadly part. The queue records which damage cards were applied and prevents routine repeat application. Manual damage controls are for explicit GM corrections; a queued card cannot also be manually applied.

Injury and Dying follow-up

If HP is lost, resolve the Injury Save at the end of the Round against remaining HP. The system posts a follow-up card; Injury Save is also on Combat. Confirm the Injury type with the GM. When Dying, use Dying: Lose 1 HP this Round once per Round and End Turn: Dying Save against remaining HP, with -1 per Injury. Stable suspends this process until new Wounds remove it. Failure of an ordinary Dying save kills the sleeve while preserving the stack. Severe Organic Damage and Real Death use a separate GM-adjudicated procedure.

Mitigation and rest

With Wounds queued, Mitigate with SP can replace them with loss of 1 HP and an Injury. The escalating cost is 1, 2, 4, 8… SP during a session and requires three Speed Dice. Borrowing dice from a future Turn is explicitly recorded by the GM. The GM resets the escalation at the start of a new session.

Clinical provides natural and medical rest. Short-rest recovery uses Endurance/Toughness; long-rest TR equals remaining HP. Squalor blocks natural healing and Poisoned blocks Short Rest Wound recovery. Clearing an Injury or healing HP still follows its treatment and duration rules.

Core references: pp.132–139.

pages.name: 07 — Loadout and Resource Catalog
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Loadout: equipment during play

Equipment records

Expand an item to read its description, Damage, Defense, Protection, Capacity, Depletion, Special Rules, Triggered Effects and upgrades. State chooses Carried, Equipped, Worn or Stored. Armor contributes only while Worn; most other effects require Equipped. Body Slots and illegal layering are checked. Stored gear is outside your carried load; re-equip it before use.

Use, Depletion and resupply

Attack runs a weapon action. Use with Skill runs a device/software Check and its Depletion. Clinical Procedure handles drugs, including doses and administration. +DP records a published use cost. Reload / Resupply removes DP only after paying the relevant printed Reload, Recharge or Request cost. An item stays Exhausted if DP still meets or exceeds Capacity.

Workbench and catalog

Equipment Workbench validates Tech Points, upgrade kits and chassis limits. Core Gear browses the official catalog and adds an item. Gear with multiple damage profiles asks for the specific source formula. The Resource Catalog tracks Capacity, DP, Price Level and procurement restrictions. Wealth is abstract purchasing power; Contacts and Networks can satisfy Requests. Descriptions and model totals are protected by Edit Sheet.

pages.name: 08 — Networks and contacts
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

Networks: people and institutions

Contacts and relationships

Open a named Contact or Relationship to read the character-facing history, current standing, affiliation and revealed identity information. These records describe whom your character knows and why they matter. They do not automatically give ownership of the linked NPC. Hidden identities and unreleased investigation information remain under GM control.

Networks and Requests

Networks show the organization, Request Level, bonus, categories and availability. A Request normally spends IP and may exhaust a Contact or Network according to its result. Agree the request and category with the GM and use the system’s Request tools. Do not simply edit IP to declare a request successful. A Scandal may restrict support or change IP costs.

Campaign-specific releases

Cold Storage imports known contacts, previous lives and relationships. Your GM releases recognition, evidence and memories as the investigation progresses. If an ONI interface is installed, its messages and releases are additional campaign tools. This journal contains no Cold Storage solution or concealed identity spoilers.

pages.name: 09 — Current Sleeve and Sleeve Archive
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

More: sleeve panels

Current Sleeve

Use More → Current Sleeve to inspect the body’s type, quality, Strength, Perception, Health maximum, acquisition history, appearance and augment capacity. The active marker identifies the body supplying your physical statistics. Edit a sleeve record only when its base values need correction; routine HP and Wounds are changed in the top resource strip.

Activating a different sleeve

Activate Sleeve archives the previous body and changes the physical statistics and HP/Wounds for the new one. It can apply psychological transfer costs. A new body does not restore the mind’s Ego automatically. Religious Coding, AI restrictions and unusual transfers require the published exceptions and GM approval.

Sleeve Archive

Use More → Sleeve Archive for former bodies, dates, circumstances of loss, remembered appearance and complications. Archived sleeves are historical records; they do not contribute the current body’s physical Attributes. Treat historical details as information your character has recovered or been given.

pages.name: 10 — Traits, Baggage and Evidence
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

More: persistent abilities and discoveries

Traits & Baggage

Expand a Trait to read its tree, branch, Tier, SP cost and effect. The system applies supported numeric clauses when their conditions match. Ask GM: Trait ruling covers contextual or narrative clauses. A Trait showing a numeric mapping is not a claim that every clause is automatic. Use Level Up for purchases and prerequisites. Baggage records long-term consequences; source-backed one-time Baggage resolution is a GM action and does not recharge resources.

Specialisations

Specialisations remove the specified missing-training Difficulty. They do not erase normal range, environmental or injury penalties. Use Level Up to purchase them, or Edit Sheet to correct a record.

Evidence & Memories

Use More → Evidence to open clues and memory records. Verified and Recovered labels are investigation state, not permission to infer unrevealed facts. The GM controls when evidence is supplied and what secrets are exposed. Take notes on what the character knows, what is suspected and what remains unconfirmed.

pages.name: 11 — Worked examples and help
pages.content:
PLAYER SHEET GUIDE · v2.5.0

A first-session reference

A normal successful Check

Perception 40 gives PB4. A Firearms Skill at Level 3 uses d8. Without other modifiers, TR is 4. A result of 3 gives +1; 4 also gives +1; 6 gives -2. A natural 1 is an Ace with +3 and the firearm Ace benefit.

An Ace firearm attack

Your firearm deals d6+PB and has Accuracy 1. With PB4, you roll a natural 1 and declare two Hits. The target declines defense. Damage is (d6+4)+(d6+4)+4: two complete Hits plus the Ace’s extra PB Wounds once for the attack. If the target instead makes a Save, repeated Accuracy adds 1 Difficulty; their positive Degrees can reduce the attacker’s available Degrees before Damage.

Where to find help

Sheet Guide opens this journal. Rules opens the Core reference. Clinical covers drugs, recovery and Virtual. Combat opens the tactical console. Ask your GM when a conditional Trait, model upgrade, Damage profile or fiction-dependent effect is not safely automatic. The 2020 Core Rulebook is the primary rules authority; Quick Start is secondary.

When a button seems unavailable

Confirm that you own the character, have targeted the right token, have the required Skill and equipment, and retain the required Speed Dice. A Damage button waits for the defense response. An Exhausted item needs a legal reload or resupply. A Hidden or Incapacitated state changes what can be done. New system code requires a full reload of each client after installation.

Boarding and travelling in vehicles

Move your PC token alongside a vehicle on the current scene. Right-click the vehicle token and click the car icon (Board vehicle / choose seat). Choose your character if several can board, then pick an empty Driver, Gunner, Operator or Passenger seat. Your PC token shrinks into its seat. Repeat for other characters. You can also right-click your own token to get in, change seat or get out. Once aboard, the vehicle and all seated PC/NPC tokens move together; only the driver (if permitted) or the GM controls the vehicle. A GM must be online for boarding and movement of occupied vehicles.
